We’ve attached a short excerpt from our logs (sample ids). We’d like to put payment on hold until we reconcile the discrepancy. Please advise next steps and whether Redwood can provisionally credit an obvious overage while this is investigated.

Thanks,
Lina

Thanks — I pulled the per-request export and an initial sample. A few notes up front:

1) Attached: usage-export-2026-07-01_2026-07-31.csv (CSV, per-request rows), sample-telemetry-ids.txt (the ids you sent), and a short draft credit note.

2) Root cause (preliminary): During 07/14 02:00 — 07/16 16:00 UTC we had an autoscaling rebalance in the EU region that triggered a short-lived double-counting edge case for streaming tokens on a subset of older session IDs. The runtime team applied a patch on 07/16 17:05 UTC that corrected the counting. We’ve flagged all sessions with the affected kernel version and marked ~12k requests as candidate double-counts.

3) VAT: the invoice taxes were applied at the account level for your EU entity (reverse-charge not applied). Per your request, column "tax_jurisdiction" in the export shows the jurisdiction tag; we can re-issue a VAT-broken invoice once we confirm jurisdiction mapping on your side.

4) Next steps we propose:
  - Immediate provisional credit for the candidate double-count token volume (we estimate 18% of the disputed window).
  - Deliver a 100-request sample (attached rows) with request_id, timestamp, model, tokens_in/tokens_out, and kernel_version for your independent verification.
  - Follow-up with a final corrected invoice or credit-note within 5 business days after you confirm samples.

Lina — attaching the exports now (links below). I’ll start the provisional credit draft and ping finance for a soft hold on collections until reconciliation is complete.

Marissa Cole
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
